 © 2026 Yahoo. All rights reserved. Richard Sherman admitted that the Indianapolis Colts' current situation is much worse than what he initially thought. 
 The franchise currently has a 2-7 record and is in the middle of a five-game losing streak. After losing to the then-winless Miami Dolphins, the team fired General Manager Chris Ballard.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement This led to a series of big trades, including Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner. They were also looking to trade running back Jonathan Taylor, but ended up keeping the three-time Pro Bowler.
 The NFL legend was discussing the Colts' game against the Dallas Cowboys from last weekend, when he was given a reality check about the AFC South team.
 "The Colts didn't even go in thinking they would have a chance to win that game. They're trying to figure out which top-five pick they're going to be picking in next year's draft out of these college quarterbacks," said Sherman on The Richard Sherman podcast.
 He was then informed by his co-host about the Colts having traded away both their first-round picks for Sauce Gardner. This then led Sherman to make a worrying admission.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement "Well, they probably should have traded Jonathan Taylor for a first-round pick, but whatever. This is why I don't run things. Wow. Wow. The Colts are in a worse spot than I thought," Sherman added.
 The Colts' only chance of getting a first-round pick for next season was to trade for Jonathan Taylor. It is still unclear if the team was offered a first-round pick and refused it, as this now puts them in a difficult position to rebuild.
 They have more than half a season to complete, and they are likely to lose a lot of games, but that is not expected to account for any first-round pick.
 The Colts have ten picks in next year's draft, with only one being in the second round. This means the franchise will struggle to add a valuable young player who could be the face of their rebuild, thereby making things significantly harder for them going forward.
